title: Through
subtitle: Though
body: Haegue Yang’s largest commission in the United States, Through marks the first time an artist has conceived of works that entangle multiple galleries across Dia Beacon’s two levels. Responding to the site’s inherent dualities—light and dark, suspended and subterranean—and drawing on the ancient East Asian theory of the Five Phases (五行思想), Yang engages the building’s cardinal axes and maps their chromatic associations in traditional East Asian cultures. This bilateral presentation involves several discrete yet integrated works: An installation of dark, draped venetian blinds on the first floor is counterpointed by vertical metal louvers that are scaled and aligned to the lower-level columns, alongside a range of other dynamic elements. Throughout the exhibition, Yang variably transfigures Images (1968), a quartet by avant-garde composer Isang Yun, echoing his approach to embodying ancient entities through contemporary media. Yang’s commission complements and challenges both Minimalism’s unit-based geometries as well as Postminimalism’s fluid forms. It unfolds as an enduring inquiry into the porosity of opposing forces and the plurality of doubles, rendering movement, migration, and oscillation across cultures, histories, and states of being.
